title: Paid enablement through Stripe
description:
**Phase 3 of 5.** Blocked by waitlist triage and by the cross-account provisioning epic. Unblocks spend ceilings.

Money, wired to the organization lifecycle that already exists.

**Stripe becomes a second caller of the enable path the members CLI already calls.** OrganizationStatus was already the right shape for a billing state machine, and this epic adds no parallel subscription status:

| Stripe event | Organization status |
| --- | --- |
| checkout.session.completed | stays pending — provisioning has not happened yet |
| provisioning succeeds | enabled, and the subscription trial ends |
| invoice.payment_failed, final attempt | suspended |
| customer.subscription.deleted | suspended |
| payment recovered | enabled, through the CLI reinstate path |

**The subscription must not start at checkout.** Provisioning can take days of back-and-forth with someone's security team, and charging a monthly fee for an organization that does not exist yet is the kind of small unfairness beta customers remember. Checkout collects the one-time setup fee immediately and creates the subscription on a trial; the trial ends from the same webhook path that flips the organization to enabled.

Setup fee tiers: $500 for Path A, $1,500 for Path B, waived for the first twenty design partners in exchange for a recorded interview and permission to write up the result. A discount that can be withdrawn is worth more than a low price that has to be raised.

Terms acceptance is collected by Stripe, not implied by a checkbox that has to be defended later. The beta terms name specific things that can happen — features change without notice, data may be reset between releases, no uptime guarantee, and the deployed footprint in their account may change shape.

This is also where the join lands: the organization records the waitlist signup it came from, so every survey answer is attached to a real tenant_id from then on.

**Start with:** the webhook and the enable path. Checkout is configuration; the state machine is the part that can be got wrong.
